results.reason: The memo identifies the five-year auto-renewal and the 270/240-day notice requirement, and says missing it locks Harrowgate in. But it miscalculates the window as June 3–June 23, 2026 (about 20 days). It should end around July 3 (240 days before Feb 28, 2027), and the memo never explains that this is effectively a 30-day window.

Issue 2 identifies the all glass and PET, any beverage, worldwide exclusivity in §3.1. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber glass, beer-only, US/Canada scope and treats Harrowgate as bound by the signed text.
Issue 6 notes receipt on August 3, 2026, that the objection period expired September 2, 2026 before the amendment date, and that the increase is deemed accepted.

Issues 3–4 explain that the amended §11.2 removes recall costs and limits the indemnity carve-out to IP claims under §9.1(c). Recall and product-defect/personal-injury exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 5 identifies new §14.4 allowing assignment to Affiliates or successors without consent. It does not say nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and it does not explain that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.

Issue 10 states that §15.2 sets the order as written amendments, then the Supply Agreement, then the Quality Agreement. It confirms the amendment qualifies as a written amendment and is applied as controlling.
Issue 3 states the cap is the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose (§11.1).
The response is a memo addressed to the Partner, with numbered issues. Each gives a 'Where' (document and section) and a 'Recommended fix'.
It proposes specific drafting, including a revised §2.2 renewal clause, a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2 and a revised §14.4.
The memo concludes the 14% increase is deemed accepted and binding, with the window closed.
The memo treats the broader §3.1 as binding and recommends renegotiation rather than claiming the term sheet governs.
